# Reviewed braces security derivative

This private package derives from the npm braces 3.0.3 tarball and preserves its MIT license and author attribution. SOURCE.json records the npm integrity, source commit, and original/patched file digests. PATCH.diff is the complete code/metadata delta; this is not an official braces release.

GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm affects every published braces version through 3.0.3. The public master commit recorded in SOURCE.json still has recursive compile/expand/stringify walks without a nesting ceiling. The package now rejects more than128 brace/parenthesis containers with SyntaxError code ERR_BRACES_MAX_DEPTH before recursive processing. Its parser counts actual syntax containers, preserving quoted and escaped delimiters. An iterative AST check protects compile, expand, and stringify when a caller supplies an AST directly, including a cyclic child graph. Expansion does not mutate an over-depth AST before refusal. The ceiling is fixed and cannot be disabled by options; the existing input-length and range limits remain in force.

Ordinary patterns, alternatives, ranges, flags and the CommonJS public API retain braces3.0.3 behavior. The package's original README describes that API. Very deeply nested patterns now fail with a controlled syntax error instead of exhausting the engine stack. This patch addresses nesting exhaustion; it does not claim to bound arbitrary caller-selected combinatorial expansion or arbitrary JavaScript getters.

The website declares braces as a direct dependency on file:../vendor/npm/braces-3.0.3-hermes.1.tgz and overrides braces with $braces. The direct declaration anchors the artifact path at the website root, including nested consumers. The tarball materializes the module beside its dependencies instead of linking outside the website module tree. Regenerate the lock and install with lifecycle scripts disabled. Regression tests resolve the actual website micromatch/chokidar consumer paths to verify that they load this implementation. Retire this derivative after a maintained upstream release carries an equivalent fix, the website resolves it, and those invariants pass.
